units: <cite ref="Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 32:15">Pirké d’R. El. ch. XXXII</cite> <he>עד שאני בעוֹדִי אברכך</he> while I am yet in my strength (of mind, able to dispose), I will bless thee.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 9:3:10">Y. Kil. IX, 32ᶜ</cite> top <he>ואין ע׳</he> and none more (shall be buried here).
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 6:4:4">Y. Erub. VI, 23ᶜ</cite> <he>ע׳ היא דבית שמאי</he> this is still in agreement with the opinion of Beth Sh.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Peah 3:7:14">Y. Peah III, 17ᵈ</cite> bot. <he>ולא ע׳ הוא בריא</he> when he is no longer well; <he>ולא עוֹדֵהוּ וכ׳</he> when he is no longer ill.

<cite ref="Tosefta Mikvaot 5:12">Tosef. Mikv. V, 12</cite> <he>עודהו הראשון וכ׳</he> (not <he>עדיהו</he>) while the first bather is yet in the water; [<he>במים</he>] … <he>עוֹדֵיהוּ רגלו</he> while the first is still with one foot in the water; <cite ref="Chagigah 19a:13">Ḥag. 19ᵃ</cite>.
<cite ref="Tosefta Keilim Metsia 5:5">Tosef. Kel. B. Mets. V, 5</cite> <he>מפני שעודיהו כלי וכ׳</he> (not <he>שענדיהו</he>) because it is still a utensil, the girls sitting therein &c.
<cite ref="Shabbat 151b:11">Sabb. 151ᵇ</cite> <he>ועוֹדְךָ בידך</he> (Ms. M. <he>ועדיין</he>) and while thou art yet in thy own power (while thou canst still dispose of thyself, s. supra).
Ib. 43ᵃ בעוֹדָן עליו when they are yet on it; שאין עודן עליו when they are no longer on it; a. fr.—ולא ע׳ אלא and no more? But (also this), and not only this, but even more.
Ib. 7ᵇ; Meg. 6ᵇ; a. fr.—מִבְּעוֹד while there is yet, during.
<cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 1:5">Sabb. I, 5</cite> <he>כדי שישורו מ׳ יום</he> in time to be soaked through during day-time (before sunset).

<cite ref="Yoma 81b">Yoma 81ᵇ</cite> <he>מתחיל ומתענה מ׳ יום</he> he must begin the fast in day-time; a. fr.—[<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Deuteronomy 13:7">Targ. Y. Deut. XIII, 7</cite> <he>בעודך</he>, read: <he>בעוּבָּךְ</he>, v. <cite ref="P00174"><he>עוּבָּא</he></cite>.]
